text:
lucy: Heads-up: ServeCraft just launched a banner claiming 'zero-config inference on any stack' with a shiny latency curve. Need a tight internal counter + SDR soundbites by tomorrow AM. :eyes:

mona: ugh. can someone grab screenshots and the landing copy?

jared: pasted screenshots. claim highlights: 'zero-config', 'one API for all hardware', and a chart comparing p50.

kevin: framing idea: 'zero-config' sells simplicity but hides tradeoffs — model shape, KV caching, batching, and kernel selection still matter for real app latency/cost.

priya: SDR 1-liners (short):
- Tech buyer: 'We tune runtime to your model and workload so production apps get consistent latency.'
- Biz buyer: 'Predictable latency and controllable unit costs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.'

lucy: shorten tech line to 'Runtime tuned to your workload for predictable latency.' keep biz line as-is.

mona: webinar micro-slide (3 bullets):
1) Serving-first optimizations: kernel selection, batching, KV caching
2) Cost levers: batching, caching, quantization suggestions
3) Ops-grade observability: token-level cost & latency breakdowns

jared: can we add a one-sentence note under slide: 'Claims like "zero-config" hide per-workload tuning that drives tail latency and cost.' keep it plain.

kevin: legal note: avoid 'lower tail latency' phrasing. use 'improved latency' or 'more predictable latency'.

priya: action items:
- @jared: write two SDR snippets (tech + biz) and drop in Notion by 10am PT tomorrow
- @mona: design 1-slide webinar frame with the 3 bullets + 1-sentence callout by COB today
- @kevin: quick legal check on 'predictable latency' phrasing and flag any no-go words

ops-bot: Reminder set: Notion snippets due 10:00 PT tomorrow (channel: #marketing).

lucy: thanks team  keep everything one short sentence, no claims we can't back up. :thumbsup:
